title: Comment box in the wrong place — after the fix

steps.page: What you asked for, and what you got
steps.intro: One row per thing you asked for, in your own words.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: What you asked for, and what you got

calls.call: The new-comment box opens right under the words you picked, never in the bottom-left corner.
calls.why: It now sits under the new comment's highlight instead of under your text selection, which adding the comment often wiped out.
calls.decided: comment boxes sometimes show up in weird places, like the bottom left

calls.call: Word files and second comments work too: the cases that failed almost every time.
calls.why: A comment on words right next to an existing highlight now gets its own highlight, and the box sits under it.
calls.decided: please investigate further to see if there's anything else you may have missed

steps.intro: Click a picture to open it large; drag on it to comment on a part.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: Every screen that changed

calls.call: A markdown file
calls.why: Box under the highlight instead of over the table at the bottom left.

calls.call: A Word file, commenting next to an existing highlight
calls.why: Before: no highlight and the box at the bottom left. After: the words are highlighted and the box sits under them.

steps.intro: What happens now when you add a comment, in order.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: What happens when you press Add comment

calls.call: The comment is created and its words are highlighted.
calls.why: Each highlight now finds its words even after another highlight on the same line cut them apart, so both get drawn.

calls.call: The box is placed under that highlight, or just above it when there is no room below.
calls.why: Your text selection is no longer needed, so it no longer matters that it disappears.

calls.call: The box stays inside the part of the file panel you can see, clear of the Edit button.
calls.why: Before, it could go anywhere in the window, including over the chat box.

calls.call: If you scroll while typing, the box moves with its words.
calls.why: When the words scroll out of view, the box waits at the panel's edge.

steps.intro: Things you could notice that I decided without asking.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: Choices I made

calls.call: The box lines up with the left edge of the highlight. When the highlight wraps onto a second line, that is the start of the line.
calls.why: The same rule the card you see when hovering a highlight already uses, so the two match.

calls.call: The box follows its words when you scroll.
calls.why: You named this as a small new behaviour; say here if you would rather it stayed put.

calls.call: If a comment's words cannot be highlighted (only in files too large to check), the box opens at the top-left of the panel.
calls.why: Before, this case went to the bottom-left corner. Without a highlight there is nothing to sit under.

calls.call: The hover card on an existing highlight also stays inside the visible panel now.
calls.why: It shares the same placement code. Before, near the bottom of the panel it could hang below what you can see.

calls.call: Code files' comment box follows its line when the editor scrolls, too.
calls.why: It uses the same box, so it got the same behaviour.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: Checks I ran, and what they showed

calls.call: New automatic check: comment twice in a markdown file and twice in a Word file, then measure the box, also after scrolling.
calls.why: Uses the app's real screens and a real click. Passed 3 runs in a row; on the old code both versions fail, one with the box at exactly your screenshot's spot.

calls.call: New tests: two comments on one line, and one comment inside another, both keep whole highlights.
calls.why: The first fails on the old code; both pass now.

calls.call: The full desktop check suite: types, tests, dead code, lint, all 571 screens, all saved click paths.
calls.why: All passed. The screens check first failed to download a helper; it passed once that was fetched.

calls.call: A fresh reviewer read the finished change.
calls.why: Found three things worth fixing and two to confirm with you; all are listed below under Found in review.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: What changed while building

calls.call: The box sits under the new highlight, stays inside the visible panel, and follows scrolling.
calls.why: As proposed in chat.

calls.call: Also fixed: a comment next to an existing highlight on the same line got no highlight at all.
calls.why: The new automatic check found it; it was the real reason Word files and second comments failed.

calls.call: Review follow-ups: nested comments, scroll cost and closed code editors.
calls.why: A fresh reviewer found these after the first build; all three are fixed and every check was run again.

steps.path: Open a file, select some words, press Add comment
steps.headline: Found in review

calls.call: When one comment sat inside another, the outer one's highlight was cut short.
calls.why: Fixed: each highlight now follows its words wherever drawing moved them. A new test covers both orders.

calls.call: The box re-measured itself whenever anything in the app scrolled, even the chat.
calls.why: Fixed: it now reacts only to scrolling that can move its words.

calls.call: A code file whose editor had just closed could have been measured.
calls.why: Fixed: a closed editor is skipped and the box stays where it was.

calls.call: When a comment's words cannot be highlighted, the box opens at the panel's top-left.
calls.why: Kept, and listed under Choices I made. It only happens in very large files.

calls.call: When its words scroll out of view, the box waits at the panel's edge rather than hiding.
calls.why: Kept, and listed under Behind the scenes; say if you would rather it hid.
